---
name: format-before-editing
description: Run prettier on the files you are about to touch BEFORE editing (many files in ziiz are prettier-dirty at HEAD), and commit that as a separate style-only commit so the real diff stays clean.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On the phase 2 prose-layer pass (2026-09-03) I formatted only after editing. All nine touched files were already failing prettier at HEAD, so the diff carried 78 lines of `@apply` class reordering in theme.css next to the real change. Nafis asked "did you run prettier before making any changes?" and chose to split it into a format-only commit followed by the feature commit.

**Why:** ziiz has ~120 prettier-dirty files (see [[pnpm-format-rewrites-whole-repo]]), so any post-hoc format of a touched file drags unrelated churn into the review diff.

**How to apply:** Before the first edit, run `pnpm exec prettier --check` on the files you plan to touch; if any fail, `--write` them and commit as `style: format ...` first. Then make the change. Keep formatting to touched paths only.
---
name: pnpm-format-rewrites-whole-repo
description: "`pnpm format` in ziiz runs prettier --write over every ts/tsx file in the repo (~120 prettier-dirty at HEAD), so it dumps unrelated churn into any diff."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3df50d4b-28e0-4406-aa50-0a535cf16830
  modified: 2026-09-04T09:43:46.713Z
---

The root `package.json` script `format` is `prettier --write "**/*.{ts,tsx}"`. The repo has roughly 120 files that fail `prettier --check` at HEAD, so running the script rewrites files far outside the change being made.

**Why:** an unrelated-formatting diff drowns the real change in review and makes the commit unrevertable in isolation.

**How to apply:** never run `pnpm format`. Format only the paths you touched: `pnpm exec prettier --write <files>` (from the repo root, so the tailwind prettier plugin config applies). If it was run by accident, recover with `git checkout -- <untouched paths>` or `git stash` the intended edits first, `git checkout .`, then pop. Pair with [[format-before-editing]].
---
name: no-commit-or-pr-unless-asked
description: "In ziiz, leave finished work uncommitted in the working tree; Nafis commits and opens PRs himself unless he explicitly asks for a commit or PR."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 191672e4-61a8-4408-bb04-9ad928279e04
  modified: 2026-09-04T10:13:12.866Z
---

On 2026-09-04, after the phase 2 prose-layer implementation passed checks, I committed it on a feature branch and was about to open a PR. Nafis interrupted: "do not commit, do not make PR." The commit was soft-reset back into the working tree.

**Why:** Nafis reviews the diff in the working tree and decides on commit shape and PR timing himself; an unasked commit adds a step to undo.

**How to apply:** for ziiz work, stop after verification with changes left uncommitted (a feature branch is fine). Commit or open a PR only when the request says so. Related: [[closed-pr-means-start-fresh]], [[format-before-editing]].
---
name: decision-logs-final-state-only
description: "Nafis wants decision logs (MIGRATION.md and similar) to record only the final state — one consolidated row per component/decision, no superseded or intermediate rows."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b011efef-6a2f-48b8-8344-0fb7813266aa
  modified: 2026-08-15T05:42:53.764Z
---

During the ziiz button migration pilot (2026-08-15), the focus-ring decision churned three times (offset ring gray-600 → gray-1000 → reverted to shadcn halo) and each change got its own MIGRATION.md row, plus one row per judgment call. Nafis asked to collapse everything to "only one — the final state of the migration."

**Why:** The log is a reference for future passes, not a diary; superseded rows force readers to reconstruct which decision actually holds, and per-call rows for a single component bury the outcome.

**How to apply:** When a decision is revised, rewrite its existing log row in place rather than appending a superseded-by chain. When a component's migration finishes, log it as one consolidated final-state row. Rejected alternatives get at most a one-clause "tried and rejected — don't revisit" note inside the final row or the relevant skill decision (as done in [[migrate-component]]'s decision 3). Same instinct applies to skill/playbook text: keep instructions current-state, purge outdated steps rather than annotating around them.

content.text:
apps/www/content/docs/colors.mdx:46:If a component's default background is Background 1 — the page surface showing through, like ghost buttons, menu items and tab chips — the ladder shifts down a rung: Color 1 is the hover background and Color 2 the active background. Components that rest transparent take that shift on the alpha scale, so the state reads over any surface.
apps/www/content/docs/colors.mdx:48:Two refinements hold on both ladders. A transient open state (`aria-expanded`, `data-open`) pins to the hover step — the highlight lives in the popup, so the trigger only ever looks hovered. And hovering an already-selected control deepens one step further (`gray-alpha-300` on the alpha ladder, `gray-950` on the inverted fills) so selection never swallows the hover response.
apps/www/content/docs/colors.mdx:64:In practice, borders default to the alpha scale; alpha hairlines hold up over any surface. Bordered controls and text fields step the hairline to Color 5 on hover — for fields, that border step is the entire hover response. Color 6's "active border" role is filled by the focus signature: solid gray-600 replaces the hairline on focus rather than stepping the alpha scale.
apps/www/content/docs/materials.mdx:12:In-page surfaces in the component library are flat by decision: cards, sidebars, inputs and wells draw a hairline `border-gray-alpha-400` on `bg-background-100` and carry no shadow, so no `ui` component uses a Surface material today. The tiers remain available for content that genuinely needs to lift off the page — marketing sections, dashboards, previews — and for consumers whose surfaces are not flat.
